text:
alex: opened a short PR to tidy up the audit-log examples and add a migration note for customers moving from Dedicated -> Private. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/3167
priya: awesome — can you call out the exact TTL semantics we expect from the ingest pipeline? customers were confused by 'retention' vs 'export' language last time.
alex: good call. I added a small section 'TTL vs archival' that says: ingest TTL = how long live logs are accessible in query; archival/export = long-term evidence store. also added example command for export.
jonah: quick read: legal flagged the phrase 'we purge customer logs after X' as potentially problematic for SOC2 wording. @legal-ops can you suggest an alternative?
legal-ops: prefer phrasing that focuses on controls and customer's configuration. suggestion: "Logs are retained per configured retention windows; Redwood provides built-in export and archival controls and can assist with legal hold requests." avoid 'we purge' and 'we delete on X' as standalone statements.
alex: updated wording per that. replaced two inline occurrences and left an explicit example showing how to set retention in the console.
chris: docs-bot link check failed on one of the SDK snippet links -> 404 for the TypeScript example.
docs-bot: :warning: link-checker: 1 broken link: /sdk/examples/ts/audit-export.ts (404)
alex: thanks — that's the file I renamed locally. pushing fix now. also added an inline minimal TypeScript snippet and a matching Python snippet for parity:
```python
# export audit events to S3 (example)
from redwood import AuditClient
client = AuditClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
client.export(scope="tenant:acme", since="2025-01-01", dest_uri="s3://acme-audit-exports/")
```
priya: can we also add a short migration checklist for Dedicated->Private? customers want step-by-step: 1) snapshot audit exports 2) verify KMS keys 3) enable private control plane export permissions. keep it as a bullet list.
alex: added a 4-step checklist and a note about KMS/HSM compatibility. also noted that export artifacts are JSONL and include a 'redwood_audit_version' field to help automated ingestion.
jonah: legal ok with the new phrasing — thanks. one ask: please add a subtle note that audit events containing tenant identifiers may need pseudonymization depending on the customer's own data policy.
legal-ops: confirming — add a suggested pseudonymization example (hashing tenant id) and a cross-link to the privacy playbook.
alex: added a tiny code example for pseudonymization and linked to /docs/privacy/pseudonymization. fixed the TS link. re-ran link-check -> green.
docs-bot: :white_check_mark: all checks passed (link-check, lint, snippet-run smoke).
priya: small nit — in the Python snippet change `client.export` param name from `dest_uri` to `destination` to match the SDK.
alex: good catch, updated. ready for review and merge unless anyone wants more changes.
chris: lgtm from eng docs side.
jonah: lgtm from security. I'll queue the legal approval stamp now.
legal-ops: approved. please include the PR number in the compliance evidence pack.
alex: PR merged. will backfill a short changelog entry for the release notes. :tada:
